title: Pure states are optimal for total energy-constrained quantum channel discrimination
abstract: We consider the discrimination of two quantum channels acting on bosonic modes, with a probe state of fixed mean photon number and no ancilla. We prove that pure probes are optimal: for every mixed probe there is a pure probe with exactly the same mean photon number that performs at least as well. The result holds for arbitrary channels and for every figure of merit built from the Chernoff quantities $\Tr[ρ_1^sρ_2^{1-s}]$, including the quantum Chernoff exponent, as well as for the single-shot error probability. The proof relies on a decomposition of any state of mean photon number $\nb$ into pure states of mean photon number exactly $\nb$, which extends a matrix rank-one decomposition of Huang and Zhang to density operators of infinite rank.
summary: This paper proves that when discriminating between two quantum channels acting on bosonic modes under a fixed mean photon number constraint, the optimal probe state must be pure. The proof utilizes a novel decomposition of mixed states into pure components, extending prior mathematical results to infinite-dimensional systems. This establishes a powerful theoretical limit on measurement performance in quantum communication.
main_problem: The paper addresses determining the optimal probe state for discriminating between two quantum channels acting on bosonic modes, subject to a fixed mean photon number constraint.
main_result: It is proven that pure probe states are optimal for this discrimination task, meaning any mixed probe can be matched in performance by a pure probe with the same mean photon number.
method: The proof relies on decomposing any state with a fixed mean photon number into a mixture of pure states, extending a known rank-one decomposition to infinite-rank density operators.
model_or_system: The system involves bosonic modes subjected to two quantum channels ($\mathcal{N}_1$ and $\mathcal{N}_2$). The probe state $ho$ is constrained by its total mean photon number $	ext{Tr}[\hat{n}ho] =  ar{n}$.
key_observables: Quantum Chernoff exponent ($\xi_Q$), single-shot error probability ($P_e$), and the mean photon number ($ ar{n}$).
important_parameters: The fixed mean photon number $ ar{n}$ acts as the primary constraint parameter.
main_assumptions: The result holds for arbitrary quantum channels and any figure of merit derived from the Chernoff quantities. A key assumption is the validity of the state decomposition lemma.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem setup, proves a crucial decomposition lemma for states with fixed mean photon number, and then uses this lemma along with properties of the Chernoff quantities to prove the optimality of pure states.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical result about optimal measurement strategies in quantum optics and quantum information, showing that purity is sufficient for optimal discrimination under energy constraints.
